decks.domain: Tests, permits, skills test and renewal

cards.front: What can happen if staff doubt your physical fitness to drive?
cards.back: Staff ask a few general health questions, and doubt about your physical fitness to drive can hold the application pending a reexamination with more medical information.

cards.front: What happens if you need glasses or contacts to pass the vision test?
cards.back: If you need glasses or contacts to pass the vision test, your license will require you to wear them while driving.

cards.front: What follows if you fail the vision test?
cards.back: Failing the vision test means an eye-care specialist must complete a vision statement, and limits such as daylight driving only may follow.

cards.front: How early must you arrive for a knowledge test toward an original license?
cards.back: For a knowledge test toward an original operator’s, chauffeur’s or commercial license, arrive at least one hour before the office closes.

cards.front: On which written tests may a foreign language interpreter help?
cards.back: Knowledge tests come in many languages, and foreign language interpreters may help on every written test except commercial license knowledge tests.

cards.front: What may a skills test interpreter do, and where is one not allowed?
cards.back: Hard-of-hearing or non-fluent applicants may use an interpreter in the skills test, who must show photo ID and only relay the examiner’s instructions, but not in commercial license written or skills tests.

cards.front: Can a non-fluent car applicant use an interpreter for the knowledge test?
cards.back: Interpreters may assist on every written knowledge test except commercial license tests, so a non-fluent car applicant can use one for the knowledge test.

decks.domain: Tests, permits, skills test and renewal

cards.front: How long is a TIP valid, and what does it let you do?
cards.back: A temporary instruction permit (TIP) is valid for one hundred eighty days and lets you practice with a licensed adult before the driving skills test.

cards.front: Who receives a temporary instruction permit?
cards.back: TIPs go to people never licensed, foreign license holders seeking a Michigan license, and people whose license expired at least four years ago.

cards.front: What must you do to get a TIP?
cards.back: To get a TIP you bring the four proofs, pass the vision test and health standards plus the written knowledge and road sign tests, pay the fee and have your photo taken.

cards.front: How long must you practice on a TIP before the skills test?
cards.back: You must practice on a TIP for at least thirty days before the driving skills test, and an adult driver education course is encouraged.

cards.front: After your skills test results arrive, how can you drive until the license comes?
cards.back: After the department receives your skills test results, your license is mailed, and a temporary operator’s permit printed from your MiLogin account lets you drive until it arrives.

cards.front: Which is required on a TIP: thirty days of practice or an adult driver education course?
cards.back: The thirty-day TIP practice minimum is a firm requirement on the TIP page, and the adult driver education course is only encouraged, not required.

decks.domain: Tests, permits, skills test and renewal

cards.front: What does a motorcycle TIP allow, and does it replace the endorsement?
cards.back: The motorcycle TIP lets a new rider practice on public roads under constant supervision of an experienced motorcyclist, and it never replaces the endorsement.

cards.front: How long does a motorcycle TIP last, and how many can a rider receive?
cards.back: A motorcycle TIP lasts one hundred eighty days, and no rider receives more than two of them in a ten-year period.

cards.front: What does a motorcycle TIP require?
cards.back: A motorcycle TIP requires age sixteen, a valid Michigan driver’s license, passing the vision and motorcycle knowledge tests, and the fee.

cards.front: What supervision and limits apply to a motorcycle TIP rider?
cards.back: A motorcycle TIP rider must stay in constant visual supervision of a licensed motorcycle operator aged at least eighteen, and may not ride at night or carry passengers.

cards.front: How does the motorcycle TIP relate to the endorsement?
cards.back: A motorcycle TIP lasts one hundred eighty days and a rider gets at most two in a ten-year period, so it bridges to the endorsement rather than replacing it.

cards.front: How do the minimum ages of a motorcycle TIP rider and the supervisor differ?
cards.back: A motorcycle TIP holder must be at least sixteen, while the licensed motorcyclist supervising that rider must be at least eighteen.

decks.domain: Tests, permits, skills test and renewal

cards.front: When is a driving skills test required?
cards.back: A driving skills test is required for Level two, for never-licensed applicants eighteen or older, when your last license expired more than four years ago, or for a license from a country other than Canada, Germany or South Korea.

cards.front: What training must an under-eighteen applicant complete before the skills test?
cards.back: Under-eighteen skills test applicants need Segment two completed, Level one held at least six months, and a log of at least fifty supervised hours with ten at night, kept in The Supervised Driving Guide or the free RoadReady app.

cards.front: What record must an under-eighteen applicant have before the skills test?
cards.back: Under-eighteen applicants must also have no convictions, civil infractions, suspensions or at-fault crashes in the ninety days right before the skills test and Level two application.

cards.front: What must an applicant eighteen or older hold before the skills test?
cards.back: Applicants eighteen or older must hold a TIP before the skills test, and a thirty-day practice period may be required.

cards.front: Who gives skills tests, and who sets their fees?
cards.back: Independent businesses approved by the Secretary of State give skills tests, and since the state does not set their fees, ask about pricing before you book.

cards.front: What part of the skills test comes first?
cards.back: The skills test starts with off-street, closed-course maneuvers, and only after passing them do you take the on-road test that earns the driving skills receipt.

cards.front: What kinds of driving does the on-road portion include?
cards.back: The on-road portion includes urban, expressway, rural highway and residential driving, as described in the Driving Skills Test Study Guide.

cards.front: Which foreign licenses avoid the skills test?
cards.back: Foreign licenses from Canada, Germany or South Korea avoid the skills test, while a license from any other country requires it.

cards.front: How do teen and adult prerequisites for the skills test differ?
cards.back: Under-eighteen applicants need a clean record for the ninety days before the skills test, while adults instead need a TIP and possibly a thirty-day practice period.

decks.domain: Tests, permits, skills test and renewal

cards.front: When may a Physician's Statement of Examination be requested?
cards.back: A Physician’s Statement of Examination may be requested at application or renewal for any physical or mental condition that may affect safe driving.

cards.front: When is a physician's statement required because of lost consciousness?
cards.back: A physician’s statement is also required when the state has reason to believe you had a seizure, blackout, fainting spell or other loss of consciousness within the past six months.

cards.front: What medical history must chauffeur and commercial license holders have?
cards.back: Chauffeur and commercial license holders must have had no blackouts, fainting spells or seizures in the last twelve months.

cards.front: Who completes the physician's statement, and who reviews it?
cards.back: A physician or physician’s assistant licensed in Michigan or another state completes the statement, describing conditions and medications, and the Driver Assessment Section reviews it.

cards.front: What happens when a serious condition is reported at renewal?
cards.back: A serious condition reported at renewal leads to a driver reexamination, so start renewing several weeks early, and a restricted license for illness may bring periodic reexams.

cards.front: Where do license restrictions appear, and how long are new drivers on probation?
cards.back: Any special licensing conditions or restrictions are printed on the license, and drivers licensed for the first time are on probation for at least three years.

cards.front: How long are new drivers on probation, and is it part of GDL?
cards.back: New drivers, GDL teens included, stay on probation for at least three years, a monitoring program kept separate from GDL.

cards.front: How do the medical look-back windows for a physician's statement and for commercial drivers differ?
cards.back: A physician’s statement looks back six months for any loss of consciousness, while chauffeur and commercial license holders need twelve months free of blackouts, fainting or seizures.

cards.front: Is the three-year probation the same thing as GDL?
cards.back: Probation of at least three years is a program separate from Graduated Driver Licensing, even though teens in GDL are also on probation.

decks.domain: Tests, permits, skills test and renewal

cards.front: In what order do you change your name on your license?
cards.back: To change your name, change it with the Social Security Administration first, wait at least three business days, then bring your license and name-change proof to an office for a new license and fee.

cards.front: What must your license address match, and what does a change cost?
cards.back: Michigan law requires your license address to match your residence and your voter identification card, and address changes are free online, in person or by mail.

cards.front: What does an online address change update?
cards.back: An online address change updates your license or ID, your voter registration, and vehicle records linked to your license account.

cards.front: When do vehicles not linked to your account get the new address, and what risk comes from not reporting a move?
cards.back: Vehicles not linked to your license account get the new address only during a vehicle transaction, and failing to report a move can bring suspension or revocation.

cards.front: How do name changes and address changes differ in where they start and what they cost?
cards.back: A name change starts at the Social Security Administration and costs a fee for the new license, while an address change starts with the Secretary of State and is free.

decks.domain: Tests, permits, skills test and renewal

cards.front: How long is a license usually valid, and when does an under-twenty-one license expire?
cards.back: A license is usually valid four years and expires on your birthday in the year printed on it, except that under-twenty-one licenses expire on the twenty-first birthday.

cards.front: Where does the renewal notice go, and what does late renewal add?
cards.back: The renewal notice goes to the address on record, driving without a valid license is illegal, and renewing after expiration adds a late fee.

cards.front: Which licenses cannot be renewed?
cards.back: A suspended, revoked or denied license cannot be renewed, and renewal can be refused without a valid Social Security number or ineligibility letter and legal presence proof.

cards.front: How can you renew when no office visit is required?
cards.back: When no office visit is required, you may renew by mail, online at Michigan.gov slash SOS or at a self-service station.

cards.front: How often must you renew in person, and what happens there?
cards.back: Every twelve years you must renew in person at an office, where vision is screened and a new photo is taken.

cards.front: What should someone who stops driving do with their license?
cards.back: Someone who stops driving returns the license to an office and applies for a state ID card instead.

cards.front: Who receives a free state ID card?
cards.back: Free ID cards go to people who are legally blind, drivers sixty-five or older who voluntarily give up their license, and drivers who lose driving privileges for a physical or mental disability.

cards.front: How does an under-twenty-one license's expiration differ from a standard license?
cards.back: A standard license runs about four years to your birthday, but an under-twenty-one license ends on the twenty-first birthday no matter when it was issued.

cards.front: How often must renewal happen in person even if remote renewal is allowed?
cards.back: You may renew by mail, online or at a self-service station when allowed, but every twelve years the renewal must happen in person with a vision screening and photo.

cards.front: When do drivers sixty-five or older qualify for a free state ID, compared with legally blind people?
cards.back: A free state ID goes to drivers sixty-five or older only when they give up the license voluntarily, while legally blind people qualify regardless of age.

recap_hooks.text: Need lenses to pass, wear them to drive; fail vision and a specialist must report.
Interpreters help on every written test except commercial ones.
A TIP lasts one hundred eighty days; practice at least thirty days before the skills test.
New drivers, foreign license holders and long-expired drivers get a TIP.
Motorcycle permits bridge to the endorsement, two per decade at most.
Rider sixteen, watcher eighteen, no night riding and no passengers.
Teens need training, fifty hours and a clean ninety days; adults need a TIP.
Closed course first, then the road.
Lost consciousness in six months means a physician's statement; commercial drivers need twelve clear months.
New drivers stay on probation for at least three years, apart from GDL.
Change your name with Social Security first; address changes are free.
Licenses run about four years to your birthday; under twenty-one ends at twenty-one.
Renew remotely when allowed, but in person every twelve years.
